To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bacteria based self healing mortar can enhance the water tightness recovery of cracked concrete, and the effect of the bacteria is more pronounced in specimens subjected to wet dry cycling.

bacteria based self healing mortar can recover water tightness of cracks when subjected to wet-dry cycles, and that the recovery of the water tightness is higher than that of the reference specimens without healing agent.

the presence of the bacteria based healing agents in the mortar matrix does not affect the compressive strength and it improves the recovery of liquid water tightness of concrete, especially when subjected to cyclic wet dry conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a self healing material that can be used for the construction of structures in aggressive environments and that can recover water tightness after micro cracks occur.
the development of a new self-healing concrete based on a bacterial system that can be incorporated into a lightweight aggregate and can be applied to the production of concrete.
a new method of self healing concrete based on the incorporation of bacteria into lightweight aggregates and its effect on the recovery of the liquid tightness of the material after cracking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the self healing agent in the mortar matrix does not affect the mechanical strength of the material.

the presence of bacteria based healing agent in mortar matrix does not affect its mechanical properties but improves the recovery of water permeability after cracking when subjected to wet/dry cycles, which is the most realistic scenario for a structure in service.
the bacteria based self healing agent is effective to enhance the recovery of water permeability in concrete, but only under specific exposure conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bacteria based self healing agents are able to improve the recovery of water permeability of concrete after cracking and exposure of wet dry cycles.

the incorporation of the healing agent into lightweight aggregate mortar does not affect the compressive strength but enhances the recovery of water permeability when exposed to wet dry cycles, due to the bacterial activity.

the bacteria based healing agents are able to enhance the water tightness recovery of concrete when subjected to wet-dry cycles, but the healing agent does not affect the water tightness when the specimens are continuously exposed to water.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bacteria based self healing agent can be successfully incorporated into lightweight aggregate mortar and the recovery of water-tightness of the specimens is significantly enhanced when the specimens are subjected to wet dry cycling.
the incorporation of the bacteria based healing agents in the concrete matrix can enhance the recovery of water permeability in wet dry conditions.
the incorporation of the healing agent into the mortar matrix is a promising approach for enhancing autogenous healing of lightweight concrete.
